messages:
sam: getting a pile of p99 latency tickets from support — started ~09:12 UTC. Customers seeing 10-30s tails on /v1/generate, p95 up ~2x. anyone seeing cluster-side anomalies? :grimacing:
oncall-bot: ALERT: high_p99_latency service=runtime env=prod region=us-west triggered at 2026-03-15T09:12:40Z — p99=28.4s, error_rate=0.3%
devon: grabbing dashboards. which model and route? can you paste customer id / route?
sam: customer=acme-inc route=/v1/generate model=gpt-medium-8k variant=quantized concurrency tier=standard
maria: running prometheus queries now. quick snippets: p95(request_duration_seconds{route="/v1/generate"}) by (model) = 1.8s -> 3.9s (09:00->09:15). p99(...) = 6.2s -> 24.1s. queue_length per worker group spiked from ~10 -> 180.
aj: interesting — node metrics show all gpu-workers at ~98% utilization and CPU steal high on a few. no OOMs. some pods in deployment runtime-model-gptmed have backlog: `.status.tasks.waiting` > 100 on 3 pods.
elaine-support: we have a customer ticket with reproduction: 5 concurrent requests, long tokens (~4k), they saw two 504s and many slow responses. repro steps attached: curl --data '{"input":"...4k tokens..."}' https://api.redwood/v1/generate
devon: long token requests + high concurrency = poor tail latencies. we do admission control by estimated token cost but maybe it's misconfigured for this route. can someone run the admission control metrics?
maria: admission_controller_rejected_total{reason="over_capacity"} jumped from 0 to 420 around 09:10, but that looks like reactive — after queues grew. admission_controller_queue_size is ~150 for model=gpt-medium-8k.
aj: pulling logs from one affected pod (runtime-abc-3):
```
2026-03-15T09:09:12Z processing request id=xyz tokens=4120 ctx_len=4100
2026-03-15T09:09:14Z enqueued request id=xyz position=1
2026-03-15T09:12:02Z processing request id=xyz started
2026-03-15T09:12:36Z completed id=xyz duration=24400ms
```
This shows long queuing before processing.
devon: yep, the runtime has per-worker concurrency limit 32 and per-request exec time is long so effective queue builds. mitigation options: 1) lower per-worker concurrency to reduce queue length and tailing; 2) increase replica count for this model pool; 3) enforce stronger admission control to reject or throttle huge token requests; 4) temporarily route acme to model=gpt-medium-4k (shorter context) or to dedicated capacity.
sam: priority=customer-facing. suggest quick mitigations: 1) enable emergency admission throttle for route to reject requests with token_estimate>3000; 2) scale up replicas by +4; 3) notify support with repro mitigation. who can apply?
maria: I can flip an admission rule in ~2m. what's the exact predicate? devon?
devon: rule: if route=="/v1/generate" && model=="gpt-medium-8k" && estimated_tokens>3000 then reject with 429 + Retry-After:30s. We'll tag as emergency and log metrics.
aj: I'll scale deployment: `kubectl scale deploy/runtime-model-gptmed --replicas=10 -n runtime-prod` — applying now.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scaled deployment runtime-model-gptmed from 6 to 10 replicas by aj at 2026-03-15T09:20:12Z
maria: enabled admission rule via config service (emergency.admission.rules). patch applied.
elaine-support: letting acme know we applied throttling for very large requests and scaled up pool. they asked for ETA on full fix.
sam: immediate post-action checks: maria can you share updated p99/p95 in 5m? aj, any change in queue sizes?
maria: 09:27 snapshots: queue_length dropped from 150 -> 18, p95 down to 1.9s, p99 down to 5.6s. admission_rejected_total incremented by 310. CPU/GPU util stabilized ~85%.
aj: confirmation: worker backlog drained on previously stuck pods. no further 504s in the last 6m.
devon: good call. next steps for postmortem: - tune admission cost calc to account for total estimated compute (tokens * model_cost_factor) - add auto-scale policy based on queued_tasks metric (scale aggressively beyond threshold) - surface per-request estimated_token in telemetry for support - consider soft-fallback to a lower-context model for heavy requests
sam: I'll open the ticket and assign postmortem to eng-runtime + support. please include timeline and the exact config changes.
elaine-support: I've updated the customer with mitigation details and asked if they'd accept a short token limit. they're ok for now.
maria: saving logs and adding dashboards alerts: create alert runbook that suggests scaling + admission toggle.
devon: also add an integration test that simulates many long-token concurrent requests and verifies p99 under 10s for defined capacity.
sam: thanks all. adding notes: root cause = overloaded workers from simultaneous long-token requests + admission thresholds reacting too late. mitigations applied: admission rule, scaled replicas. follow-up: cost-based admission calc + autoscale by queue_length. closing thread and will link PMR when created.
